others.route: Work permit (Council for the Ongoing Government)

note: Tokelau: a New Zealand citizen who isn't a Tokelauan needs no permit to enter but may not stay past ten days without one and may not work without a current work permit or a special permit that authorises work; anyone else needs a permit to be in Tokelau and the same work permit to work (Immigration Rules 1991, rr. 4–5, as Tulafono a Tokelau 2016 consolidates them). A work permit lets its holder reside and work for up to three months and needs the approval of the Village Councils of all three islands; a special permit, up to three years (rr. 7, 9(3)). Tokelauans need none (r. 3), and the game holds no Tokelauan passport apart from New Zealand's, so New Zealand passports take the work permit. Read in PacLII's copy through archive.org's snapshot of 23 December 2024 (PacLII and New Zealand Legislation refuse this client); no later amendment was looked for beyond PacLII's list. No days without the permit are named.

sources.said: A New Zealand citizen who is not a Tokelauan does not require a permit to enter ... may not work in Tokelau unless that person holds a current work permit or a current special permit that authorises the person to work in Tokelau. ... A person who is not a New Zealand citizen ... may not be in Tokelau unless that person holds a current permit; ... work permits, which allow the permit holder to reside and work in Tokelau for a period not exceeding 3 months;
